We introduce a new hybrid approach that combines traditional finite difference methods with deep learning to create a highly efficient solver for the shallow water equations. This solver, termed D^2LSE, utilizes tailored loss functions to ensure accuracy in solving complex fluid dynamics problems. When applied to the 1D and 2D cases, D^2LSE demonstrates exceptional speed and accuracy, outperforming conventional finite difference and high-resolution Godunov methods by two orders of magnitude in terms of calculation time. This remarkable performance allows D^2LSE to simulate 1D shallow water equations for a million seconds in under five seconds and to handle a large-scale 2D case with high resolution in a comparable timeframe. These results highlight the immense potential of machine learning to accelerate the resolution of nonlinear PDEs in the context of shallow water dynamics.

Digital photography with an high dynamic range (HDR) combines several photos with different exposure levels to create an image with an extensive range of brightness. Traditional HDR techniques assume the best areas in underexposed and overexposed images, but this can introduce artifacts when scene content shifts between frames. This paper presents an improved approach that automatically selects the most appropriate exposures for a given frame and utilizes a linear regression method to combine them, resulting in the DRR-HDR algorithm. This algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through various high-dynamic-range scenarios, showing significant improvements over conventional HDR methods, especially in complex scenes with a high dynamic range.

Deep neural networks have extensively dominated the causal inference research, 
yet our current understanding of how neural estimators construct and utilize causal 
knowledge remains unclear. This paper aims to clarify the causal learning 
capabilities of neural algorithms by analyzing their performance under various 
estimation methods and structural representations of the causal graph, particularly 
the Pearl's three worlds and the directed acyclic graph (DAG). Through simulation 
experiments and real-world data application, our research reveals that neural models 
may inadvertently learn confounding relationships that can be described as "virtual 
cycles," which could be considered a potential limitation. However, we also propose 
two novel approaches to mitigate this issue: constrained neural optimization and 
regularized back-door adjustment optimization. Our findings could provide valuable 
guidance in utilizing modern neural methods for causal inference. To facilitate this 
application, we have opened up our simulation code for public use at this link: 
https://github.com/yuxuanliang/ccneural.

This work offers an innovative interpretation of the 1-parameter deformation of symplectic structures on the torus $T^4$, building upon the foundation established by Mumford. We incorporate an additional degree of complexity by examining the symplectic structures in relation to a fractional part $\lambda$ of Planck's constant. This perspective enables us to identify specific conditions under which the indicated 1-parameter deformation of symplectic structures on $T^4$ does not constitute a departure from the original symplectic structure, based on the B-field principle. Furthermore, we provide a collection of counterexamples to this principle's universality.

To facilitate a faster convergence in simulations using finite element methods for solving complex mechanical problems at multiple scales, effective multilevel preconditioners have been developed. This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of three multilevel preconditioners, which utilize discontinuous Galerkin, Hermitian projection, and mass assembly algorithms to topographically simplify the computation of element stresses across time elements. Our results show that these multilevel preconditioners significantly improve the efficiency of solving nonlinear mechanics problems, particularly as the size and complexity of the computational grid increases. In particular, our analysis demonstrates that using a mass-based multilevel preconditioner reduces the computational time required to solve mechanical problems on highly detailed grids from days to hours, providing a substantial acceleration compared to traditional methods. These findings have significant implications for researchers and clinicians who use mechanical models to analyze detailed physiological processes, which in turn can contribute to a better understanding of cardiovascular disease.

This study investigates the reasons for non-Gaussian diffusion observed in materials with uniformly distributed permeability through computer simulations. The findings suggest that this anomalous diffusion can arise from a variety of processes - faster or slower than typical Brownian motion - and that, in all cases, the spatial distribution of displaced particles exhibits a heavy-tailed pattern. The extent of this pattern is directly linked to the diffusion coefficients' variation range and is independent of the initial spatial arrangement of the particles. The researchers also found that the variation in diffusion coefficients, combined with the mean square displacement dynamics, can be used to make non-Gaussian diffusion patterns predictable across different scenarios.

We develop a generalized model for the linear and Kerr nonlinear interaction between optical resonator and waveguide modes. By expanding the model beyond its common model-based applications, we expand it to capture a comprehensive set of resonator modes, interacting with both anomalous and normal dispersion waveguide modes. We express all model parameters explicitly in terms of fundamental physical properties and demonstrate how various existing models can be derived from our approach. Furthermore, we identify a range of previously unexplored scenarios that can be realized using this model.

A recent study introduces a new deep learning technique to reconstruct high-resolution flow fields from low-resolution measurements, utilizing Waddington paths concepts and generative adversarial networks, and finding success in accurately recovering complex turbulent flow patterns.

Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) has seen significant advancements, but evaluating these methods poses challenges due to the complexity of automated systems. In the realm of natural language processing and computer vision, large evaluation platforms have been successfully utilized, yet RL lacks comparable infrastructure. This paper introduces L2Explorer, an innovative RL evaluation platform featuring automated learner integration, a modular design, an adaptable framework, and a centralized elasticsearch database for efficient data management. L2Explorer was tested with various RL methods across different scenarios, demonstrating its capability to streamline the often tedious task of performance assessment. This tool is intended to serve as a starting point, providing researchers in RL with an easier way to assess their methods and facilitating community feedback to further enhance its functionality. The code for L2Explorer is available on GitHub at the following link: this GitHub link.

We develop a new approach for analyzing and improving declarative process models, adding an element of dynamism to the typically static assessment method. Our innovation involves a new framework for exploring and analyzing such processes, classified into four main activities: an initial analysis phase, a simulation of processes using streams, preparation of test cases, and integration of results to refine the process model. A key process component, the monitoring and exploration engine, is designed to execute these activities, allowing for a live assessment and exploration of the process model, including identifying areas of difficulty and suggesting improvements. A practical application of this method and model is demonstrated in the context of data entry verification for an IT system.

This research paper examines the concept of compactification for the configuration space of n points on a Riemann surface of genus g, denoted as M_{0,n}(S), where the points do not intersect the surface's punctures, for genera g ≥ 2. We establish the equality of two compactification methods, specifically the geodesic compactification, denoted as \bar{M}_{0,n}^{G}(S), and the Fock-Schwinger-Ward compactification, denoted as \overline{M}_{0,n}^{FSW}(S), resulting in the relationship \bar{M}_{0,n}^{G}(S)=\overline{M}_{0,n}^{FSW}(S). Furthermore, for the case of a torus with n points, denoted as \Sigma_{1,n}, we explore the boundary behavior of the hyperbolic length of the shortest closed geodesic within the compactification \overline{M}_{0,n}^{FSW}(\Sigma_{1,n}). We demonstrate that any sequence of configurations where this length approaches zero must include a subsequence that converges to configurations satisfying specific constraints outlined in the paper.

Using star formation rate measurements from the JADES sample, a comprehensive dataset of 424 spectrally confirmed stars, we examined the relationship between mass specific star formation rates (SFR/M*) and total stellar mass (M*) for early type and late type galaxies, identified through the J-decomposition method. Traditional SFR indicators often struggle to accurately measure star formation in early type galaxies due to their old stellar populations, potentially skewing comparisons. We found that both early type and late type galaxies initially follow similar paths on the M*-SFR diagram, but diverge at masses $log(M/_{\odot}) \approx 9.8$. Specifically, we observed that lower SFR/M* values for high mass early type galaxies cannot be attributed to measurement errors. Furthermore, we hypothesis that the difference in behavior observed is rooted in the intrinsic properties of these galaxies, particularly their bulge-to-total mass ratios. We found a marginally significant correlation between lower SFR/M rates and higher bulge-to-total mass ratios for JADES galaxies, but further improvements in mass specific star formation rate measurements could potentially unlock more definitive findings.

Accurate sentiment analysis is essential for understanding user feedback across different cultural contexts. As acquiring labeled data varies in difficulty and cost across languages, this research focuses on improving few-shot sentiment analysis when limited labeled data is available for a target language. Since the source language's sentiment analysis is already established, this study evaluates two approaches to transfer knowledge from the source language to the target language: direct transfer and model transfer. Both approaches are analyzed in terms of various languages and emotion categories, considering that sentiment and emotion are distinct concepts. Furthermore, this study explores the potential of simultaneous classification of sentiment and emotion to facilitate more effective knowledge transfer. However, this approach proves particularly successful when moderate amounts of labeled data are accessible for the target language.

Studies indicate that ICU data from X-ray images is predictable, and our research reveals actionable features for predicting ICU information, including severity scores, infection duration, oxygen saturation levels, and a high probability of ICU admission.

The work in Section 3.5 demonstrates that a simplicial bundle over a space X is equivalent to a specific type of simplicial structure consisting of three components: a principal bundle of the general linear group over X, along with an associated bundle defined by the simplicial standard model. Furthermore, we establish relationships between the concepts of simplicial bundles and the Bundles of simplicial structures, providing a comparative analysis with the work of Rees regarding bundles of Lie algebras. However, a direct correlation between these concepts and Lie algebras over principal bundles, as explored in the work of Dell'Amico et al., is not feasible.

This research focuses on establishing a visual association detection task that has previously been overlooked. The primary challenge in this task is the high rate of false positives generated by the model, primarily due to the lack of meaningful background images in existing datasets. To tackle this issue, we propose incorporating external knowledge to refine the model's predictions, along with creating a novel dataset called Wikivision. This new data incorporates description captions and lists of related entities for 25k images. To effectively utilize the factual information, we develop an Entailment-based Visual Association Detection (EVAD) model, which can accurately predict associations while minimizing false positives. EVAD demonstrates superior performance compared to our previous approach on a revised COCO dataset, showing an increase in accuracy and a significant improvement in the relationship classification F1 score. Furthermore, the model's enhanced precision leads to a higher average precision (AUPR) score, particularly in challenging relationships such as 'part of' and 'type of'. The research also presents the first evaluation of background images' significance for visual association detection.

We are proposing an 'uneven disk' model to explain the rapid growth of galaxy bulges. This model is derived from findings in a galaxy cluster, and utilizes two main sources of data: observations of the galaxy's structure and its associated star formation activity. Our analysis of this data reveals that galaxy bulges form quickly through three interconnected processes. Firstly, material is accreted via violent processes, and this material is non-uniform, favoring the galaxy's center. Secondly, intense star formation occurs, and like the accreted material, it favors the galaxy's center, contributing to bulge formation directly. Thirdly, internal structure shifts, and like both of the previous processes, it contributes more to bulge formation at the center. We are drawing comparisons between this 'uneven disk' model and the major merger model used to explain galaxy bulge formation in the local universe. This analysis suggests that while bulge formation is driven by energetic events, it can result from a range of processes that favor material, star formation, and internal activity that accumulate at a galaxy's center.

On November 7, 2004, three space observatories discovered four major solar outbursts. Two of these outbursts, occurring at 05:44 UT and 06:14 UT, were particularly powerful and caused multiple types of solar radiation to release at 2.0 GSaR each. A notable observation was the detection of solar neutrons of high energy during these events. A thorough analysis was conducted on solar data, extracted from the Space Physics Research Laboratory's Geostationary Spectrometers, focusing on a specific region of the sun (250-550 degrees longitudes, 0-50 degrees latitudes). Using a program called GRB98, an eight-component model was employed to break down the detected solar neutron data into individual spectra of electrons, protons, and heavy ions.

We conducted spectrophotometric and high-resolution spectroscopic analysis of K55rd to M65rd stars, including K69, using the MK classification system. Our study revealed unexpected narrow absorption lines of Na I and Fe in these stars, providing evidence of angular momentum that is typically associated with rogue stars. Engaging in further investigation of these features, we examined their origins by analyzing the rotational velocities and positions in the effective temperature spectrum of these stars. We compared the results with other known phenomena, such as chromospheric and coronal emissions, as well as mass overflow in specific stars. However, after controlling for angular momentum and assessing the equivalent widths of Na I and Fe, we found no evidence of a disk, mass overflow, or unusual stellar activity. We found that these features were merely narrow manifestations of intrinsic stellar activity. Ultimately, we sought to explain the unusual extent of these Na I and Fe absorption lines through possible scenarios involving naive angular momentum transfer or heavy-metal opacity effects due to a BOINO.

The rapid proliferation of news online has made it crucial to effectively identify fraudulent reports. This research proposes a novel solution called Meta Neural Process Networks (MNPP) to tackle this issue. MNPP takes a two-pronged approach, initially processing multimodal data of news through a common encoder and then leveraging a meta-learning framework to train on minimal samples, allowing it to generalize effectively even with limited data. To further enhance MNPP's ability to detect counterfeit news, this research develops a new attention mechanism that captures complex relationships between multimedia news elements. Furthermore, an efficient training strategy known as meta gradient descent is employed to enhance the model's performance. Experimental results on large-scale multimedia news datasets demonstrate the superiority of MNPP in terms of both accuracy and efficiency when compared to existing methods.

This study investigates the possible discontinuities in solutions to a time-dependent equation known as a recurrent transport equation in a domain. We establish that for a specific initial condition, solutions to this equation in $L^\infty$ norm experience an infinite rise over a short time interval, regardless of how smooth the domain is. We also Examine the impact of source terms and operator coefficients on this phenomenon of sudden infinite growth.

This research develops theoretical designs for Golay complementary arrays, specifically the phase-ramp polyphase structures used in applications like radar and RFI filtering. It establishes necessary conditions for creating a set of these structures and generates a range of new designs, including those with 4 and 6 phases, and in particular, extends the known single-side lobe width limits for these designs. Additionally, this work examines an asymmetric configuration with 3 phases and establishes constraints for a 6-phase design, before concluding with an exploration of the relationship between these designs and Golay complementary primes, as well as their application to pulse compression in radar systems.

This research investigates the occurrence of valley interaction and spin transfer within silicon molecules, specifically in Si_2, SiNb_2, and SiTa_2 arranged in a hfb structure. First-principles calculations reveal that the energy separation between valley states in Si_2 can lead to interference effects, limiting electron transmission near certain bias conditions. Notably, this effect is more significant in Si_2 molecules compared to those with taq symmetry. Furthermore, possible spin transfer mechanisms are explored by evaluating the spin polarization of electron transmission in these materials.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been highly effective in various network analysis tasks such as classification, regression, and ranking. However, GNN variants often mimic simple feedforward networks, hindering their ability to model complex systems with intricate dependencies on past, present, and future data. In this study, we investigate a more challenging dataset from the NASA Jet Engine dataset, specifically focusing on the operation phases of jet engines and associated sensor readings. We establish a direct correlation between the GNN architecture and the jet engine's internal components, demonstrating that JET engines' complex non-linear dynamics can be accurately captured by a customized GNN model. This JGT-GNN achieves superior performance compared to existing methods in predicting JET engine operation stages.

In the context of rational stable homotopy theory, we establish a method to identify the rank of specific modules, which these modules represent in terms of counting certain types of mathematical structures called Lie algebras. These Lie algebras are derived from a more basic type of algebraic structure, which we refer to as "infinitesimal operads," and we're interested in those that possess a certain property called "identicality." We develop an algorithm, which in turn relies on an understanding of certain types of combinatorial objects known as permutations, that can be used to determine the rank of these modules over a specific mathematical framework, which we refer to as the Steenrod algebra. Our approach builds upon earlier research conducted by multiple mathematicians, including Lesh, Stasheff, and Tambara.

Generating medical images with specific pathologies is essential for developing and assessing medical image analysis techniques that automatically detect diseases. This study introduces a new, efficient method to generate images with lesions in the brain based on a novel neural network design. This proposed framework combines multiple components, including an iterative reconstruction module and two types of discriminators, to generate images with lesions in the brain. The results show that the proposed method produces high-quality images with lesions in the brain that are harder to distinguish from real images with pathologies. Furthermore, experimental data indicates that the proposed method generates images with lesions in the brain that are easier to detect than images with abnormalities generated by an earlier technique.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for high-performance computing, whose compilation process previously relied on manual graph transformations. This hands-on approach, although effective, is time-consuming and limited in scope, restricting GP 2's applicability to large-scale performance acceleration. To overcome these constraints, we developed the GP 2 Compiler, an automated tool that efficiently converts GP 2 representations into high-performance dependency graphs. This compiler not only expedites the GP 2 modeling process but also allows for complex transformations of graph elements. To effectively manage these transformations, the compiler incorporates a set of built-in operations capable of accurately representing performance-enhancing optimizations. We demonstrate the GP 2 Compiler's capabilities by compiling simple GP 2 representations manually optimized graphs, and in response to the Limare et al.'s evaluation feedback, we are plannning to make the GP 2 Compiler available on the HPC-Bench suite.

Recently, external resources such as knowledge graphs and Krdense have gained popularity for the purpose of providing additional information in content-based social media posts. To effectively select suitable attributes for inclusion, it is crucial to develop an efficient framework that can accurately scan and evaluate potential attributes from social media text. In this study, we introduce a novel unified model consisting of three distinct but interconnected modules - a meaning encoder, a contrastive learning module, and a score predictor - for the task of extracting attributes from social media content. Furthermore, we conduct separate experiment sets to assess the performance of our proposed framework in both standalone and collaborative settings for attribute extraction. The results from these experiments demonstrate that our model outperforms existing methods in terms of extraction accuracy.

This research paper focuses on creating infinite families of quotient groups from a specific twisted wreath product, denoted as $K_n \wr^a \beta K_m$, where the sizes of two variables, n and m, satisfy certain conditions. A family of quotient groups is identified and confirmed to have specific characteristics related to an infinite series defined by another variable, f, with a starting point of 1. A particular example of this family is confirmed to correspond to an infinite collection of specific types of quotient groups. Ultimately, the proof establishes the intrinsic properties of the defined family of quotient groups, including their intrinsic classification.

Working with categorical data on a large scale is becoming increasingly common, but the methodological tools available to analyze such data are limited in comparison to those for continuous data. To effectively work with categorical data on a large scale, it is crucial to develop penalty-based methods that leverage its underlying structure. This study makes an innovative step by developing and evaluating various Group Lasso penalty methods, specifically adapting the Firth-Lasso and Ali-Lassos for categorical data, and comparing their sparsity-inducing effects. Through the use of simulated and real-world datasets, we evaluate and rank these methods and make refined recommendations for their application. Furthermore, we successfully apply two methods that were previously unused to two high-profile datasets, expanding their analytical possibilities.

Large-scale language models achieve significant performance in numerous tasks, yet their extensive knowledge gaps remain uninspected and uninfused. Traditional knowledge infusion methods typically rely on compact knowledge graphs or summaries, which may not adequately address the extensive depth of knowledge required for these models. Our proposed framework, called SI2E, utilizes a specialized subset designed to test the ability to incorporate diverse structured knowledge sources, including a fully reconstructed knowledge graph. Furthermore, we explore various infusion strategies, including traditional structured sources like Wikibert and a unique dataset representing 1.4 million scientific insights, referred to as OneBIM. Through comparative analyses, we demonstrate the SI2E subset's suitability for evaluating structured knowledge infusion for large-scale models and explore the impact of diverse knowledge sources and infusion methods on model performance. Our findings reveal that smaller models benefit most from diverse knowledge sources and that diverse knowledge sources tend to outperform compact ones in terms of structured knowledge tasks.

This paper addresses the issue of lines undergoing spatial aliasing when drawn between map points, which can lead to the appearance of unnecessary widening or narrowing and may even create illusory branch-like formations. To solve this problem, which is particularly prevalent at high frame rate settings, we propose and analyze several anti-aliasing techniques including: filtering adjacent vertices, adjusting vertex spacing, and applying position-based filtering. Furthermore, we propose a novel method called spatial sampling with adaptive step sizes, which dynamically adjusts the interval between samples based on local angle changes, and present an optimized implementation that minimizes computational costs. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our anti-aliasing techniques in various complex scenarios.

To enhance the quality of speech on damaged audio networks, several methods using deep learning have been effective when multiple microphones are available. However, in scenarios where a single microphone is used, especially if it's located close to the speaker, traditional speech enhancement techniques may struggle to produce undesirable outcomes. We propose a novel Dual-Path Convolutional Neural Network (DPCRN) model to generate precise speech representations and subsequently enhance spoken content. This model integrates two distinct networks: one employing dual RNN modules to capture the temporal dependencies of speech and another with two bi-directional GRU components that historic and future dependencies of text transcriptions. We believe the DPCRN architecture successfully combines the benefits of both time-series and text representations, enabling it to effectively convey spoken content and provide precise temporal projections. Experimental evaluations on the LibriSpeech dataset validate the superiority of our approach over state-of-the-art single-microphone baselines, with results showing reduced error rates and indicating the duality of our model's components contributing to its performance.

To advance multi-fluid modeling of atmospheric phenomena like El Ni\~{n}o, we first need a robust single-column foundation that accurately captures multi-fluid convection. Here, we evaluate a new two-fluid rayleigh-benard convection model, confirming its correctness and consistency through comparisons with a simplified two-fluid approach. The model demonstrates accurate simulation of two-fluid convection under various thermal gradients, matching single-fluid results when fluid properties are uniform throughout the simulation chamber. These findings validate the reliability of our multi-fluid model for larger-scale atmospheric simulations.

Within the context of three Jaynes-Cummings models that do not share entanglement, we investigate and compare various patterns of atomic behavior - specifically coherent, inverted, and those exhibiting statistical inversion. By analyzing and contrasting the source and impact of these distinct dynamics, we provide insights into their underlying nature. Furthermore, we demonstrate a method to observe truly system-level entanglement between the field and the atoms, distinguishing it from the Fano-atomic entanglement present in each individual JC model. Our findings also highlight how the degree of nonlinearity can give rise to collective phenomena, with implications for areas such as collective quantum feedback.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them or other subjects.
Traditional methods for determining sentiment on social media have heavily relied on class-
based classification techniques. In this paper, we apply a novel approach using Long Short-
Term Memory networks to analyze the sentiment expressed on Twitter. Our model successfully
determines the sentiment expressed on Twitter as positive, negative, or neutral. Our
results demonstrate that our method outperforms previous models for both classification and
regression tasks.

A nonlinear interaction between scalar fields and electromagnetism can lead to a new type of black hole in an anti-de Sitter space, and this paper explores the shadow and thermal properties of these non-linear charged black holes. By calculating the quantum shadow of these black holes using the Crisostomi method and employing the McGeorge equation, we also determine their quasi-periodic orbits. Additionally, we analyze the thermodynamics of non-linear charged black holes in four and five-dimensional spaces to gain a better understanding of their thermal properties. Furthermore, we visualize the shadow of these black holes after applying a conformal transformation to the observer's space in an AdS space.

Reconstructing a state of squeezed light interacting with the thermal field of a mirror is presented using data from an experiment involving light phase shifts, and a new method for analyzing density tomograms is introduced to reveal features related to quantum entanglement and long-range interactions. As entanglement is discovered between the light and the thermal field, gradual transitions in the shape of the tomogram arise and lead to a switch from diagonal to off-diagonal patterns, which is significant. This reconstruction and analysis method is then applied to the BEMIR system, and the results show that entropy reduction can occur伴随 light phase shifts, providing an unusual example of entropy changing in conjunction with the emergence of long-range order.

In this study, forecasting user's visual focus in360-degree video travel experiences has gained significant interest. Most prior work on this issue relies on artificial markers or metadata attached to video content. In contrast, this paper's original approach uses subtitles attached to video content as input for predicting users' visual focus, without adding extraneous data. Subtitle-driven viewport forecasting for360-degree virtual travel video content is achieved in this research. Experimental results using real-world datasets show that Subtitle-driven viewport forecasting outperforms its non-360-degree counterpart and is supported by findings from real-life scenarios. In addition, this work includes practical suggestions for applying this forecasting technology in real-world settings.

We develop a decoupling theory, approximating the number of solutions to a quadratic system of inequalities and an equality, both shared by the same set of functions within a given $L^p$ space.  This inequality system and equality were initially studied by Bernstein and Rousseau.  By leveraging local geometry and extending it through an uncertainty principle, we establish a foundation for approximating these solutions, which in turn leads to a corresponding decoupling theory.  This theory decouples a curved torus from a flat torus, both lying within a flat cube.  Furthermore, it provides insights into resolving some questions related to the decoupling that appeared in the work by Guo-Li-Yu.

The research investigates the fundamental renormalon singularities in the color dipole gluon TMD parton distribution function (PDF) from first principles. Findings indicate that a specific term in the $1/Q^2$ power correction series, associated with an infrared singularity, is non-negligible. This term becomes particularly apparent in high-energy processes involving tcp interactions at very small x values in inclusive processes. This is in contrast to previous studies based on hadron shape functions or TMD factorization, which found some of these parton distribution contributions to be suppressed.

Using ultrashort laser pulses to process two-dimensional dielectric surface lattice structures generates a rich variety of lattice-induced effects, including the creation of Bloch states and the bending of light through the photonic bandgap. We investigate a sophisticated scenario where a Raman nonlinear effect in the lattice causes soliton formation. Additionally, we examine the interaction of lattice-induced surface lattice solitons and a nonreciprocal photonic lattice soliton created through the combination of nonlinearity and the Kerr effect. We also explore the coupling of lattice-induced surface lattice solitons with a vector-sensitive magnetophotonic lattice in conjunction with a quadratic nonlinearity.

Decision outcomes framework, formulated by Apple, is a black-box structure that processes decisions based on a user's needs. It allows for simple customization by altering the underlying decision rules. However, this framework cannot acquire new knowledge on its own, requiring manual configuration for each new use case. Our work presents a novel approach to teaching this framework new decisions through a supervised learning method. We developed a decision dataset, providing examples for various scenarios, and used this data to train the framework's model, enabling it to handle new tasks through few-shot or zero-shot learning. Experimental results show that this approach significantly improves the framework's performance, even when introducing completely new categories. Furthermore, we demonstrate the model's effectiveness in real-world applications, such as identifying food types for dietary restrictions and animal species for food chains, after being provided with minimal training data.

Based on previous $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ branching fraction measurements, we estimated the CP-violating difference between conjugate decay processes to be ($5.8^{+7.0}_{-5.8}$ ± 2.5) percent. Constructing the lattice of submodules of a given module is a fundamental problem in order theory, particularly when the module has the property of being multiplicity-free. A significant challenge arises when only partial information about the submodule relations is available, such as the inclusion relationships of submodules relative to the module itself. This project aims to experimentally determine the lattice of submodules of the component of the Boltzmann module within the associative envelope of the combinatorial Hopf algebras of descents, using the computer algebra system Macaulay2 as a computational tool. As a result, we have computationally verified that this lattice is isomorphic to the set of order ideals of a poset, providing a comprehensive understanding of its structure.

In a competitive environment where multiple agents operate, it's essential for them to understand and predict each other's behaviors to make informed decisions. CO-LAD, a novel approach has been developed to help these agents form accurate representations of their peers by processing shared observations and actions, allowing them to anticipate future behaviors and improve overall performance. CO-LAD agents' future predictions are crucial for effective learning, yet training future prediction models in reinforcement learning settings remains challenging due to the absence of complete data. To address this limitation, CO-LAD leverages GAN technology to create an agent-specific model that learns to reproduce future observations and actions from partially available information. CO-Observation Learning is further enhanced by introducing a representative strategy called CO-SLRG, which combines the advantages of current reinforcement learning and GAN techniques while avoiding the drawbacks of both methods. CO-SLRG's effectiveness is validated through CO-LAD's superior performance in various multi-agent tasks, including multi-agent Markov decision processes and deep learning-based games such as vector world and hunter-prey games, particularly when there are large numbers of co-observed entities in more complex environments.

Personalized codes, often denoted as PAC codes, were introduced in a series of related papers with the goal of providing a robust authentication mechanism to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks in wireless networks. Although the original proposal suggested using correlation attacks to verify PAC codes' validity, this method is impractical due to its high computational demands in real-time applications. This research introduces an efficient Matrus-like approach to assess the reliability of PAC codes, replacing the previously used method. Additionally, we investigate the code's error-detection capabilities, denoted as a(t), and establish its lower bound as 2(a). However, our findings are not directly applicable to the PAC codes' specific design, necessitating a more tailored analysis. Through a statistical analysis, we determine that the code's reliability follows a uniform distribution, denoted as U[0, 1]. Based on this discovery, we introduce new, more accurate codewords, denoted as $\text{PAC}_{new}$, which offer improved error-detection capabilities compared to the original PAC codes. We also provide a step-by-step example to clarify the entire process.

Neural machine translation (NMT) models typically generate translations sequentially, as this approach has been found to produce high-quality outputs. Nonetheless, leveraging extensive action spaces for training NMT models generates simultaneous action sequences that can improve the efficiency of inference processes. Although current NMT reinforcement learning techniques utilize extensive action spaces for training, they rely on incomplete action space sampling methods, which fail to account for all possible action space permutations. This investigation utilizes complete space sampling (CSS) reinforcement learning NMT models, comparing it to traditional incremental space sampling (ISS) NMT models across multiple datasets, including their respective simultaneous NMT baselines. Experimental results show that complete space sampling models outperform incremental space sampling models in most cases, facilitating NMT reinforcement learning models to learn efficient simultaneous translation models NMT models that operate sequentially during inference.

Researchers examined the steady-state behavior of a quantum system under varying periodic conditions, finding an interesting non-equilibrium steady state where the system's statistical properties remain unchanged over time despite lacking coherence. This rare phenomenon occurs in simple two-level quantum systems when given specific drive frequencies. Our theoretical predictions were successfully validated through careful experiments using superconducting circuits. Notably, we discovered that this non-equilibrium steady state persists even with noisy drive signals, as long as the drive frequency stays within a particular range. Both our theory and experimental data reveal that wider drive frequency intervals result in broader non-equilibrium steady state frequency windows.

A fourth-order nonlinear partial differential equation is used to describe the behavior of a bi-harmonic operator applying to a hypersurface within a Euclidean space, denoted as $\Delta^{2}f=\Delta(\Delta f)$. Researchers have been particularly interested in characterizing the properties of operators within this equation. This paper proposes new definitions for three types of operators - recurring, semi-recurring, and 1-step operators - applied to a hypersurface in a Euclidean space. Specifically, we define a hypersurface containing a recurring operator as one where $k\mathbf{H}=\Delta f$, where $\mathbf{H}$ represents the mean curvature vector of the hypersurface within the Euclidean space, and $\Delta$ is an invertible operator. Conversely, a hypersurface with a 1-step operator is described as having $ \Delta f=k\mathbf{H}$. This study aims to describe and analyze the properties of hypersurfaces that contain recurring, semi-recurring, and 1-step operators within a Euclidean space. Furthermore, we seek to characterize those operators in terms of finite type and those with polynomial growth in terms of spectral theory.

A collection of positive integers is said to be $p/q$-identifiable if, given access to a function that either returns an element from the collection or an error, a randomized algorithm can distinguish with high confidence between a frequent element (appearing at least $p/q n$ times in $n$ samples) and rare elements (appearing less than $p/q n$ times) between $p/q$ and $(P - \delta)/q$ times, where $\delta$ is a positive constant. This paper delves into the properties of collections with a specific size or under a uniform distribution, and also considers the case where the algorithm has additional knowledge of $p$, $q$, and the collection itself. Furthermore, we analyze a list of problems related to $p/q$-identifiable collections, and provide solutions to some basic cases.

MongoDB is widely used for search and indexing applications, and its performance is notable. However, ensuring data consistency across its various transactional configurations poses a challenge. This study presents a consistency validation framework for MongoDB, presenting and evaluating several approaches to detect issues that may arise. Tailing the oplog stream is presented as the most effective method, offering high sensitivity in catching problems with minimal performance impact. In comparison, other methods are found to be either less effective in maintaining consistency or too resource-intensive. Furthermore, this work contributes a set of test cases designed to expose problems resulting from flawed transactions or index operations. These test cases, when integrated into MongoDB's test suite, can help prevent future issues. Also, by applying the oplog-based validation method to existing test cases and production workloads, we demonstrate its effectiveness in maintaining consistency. This study's findings provide a foundation for developing an end-user tool to ensure MongoDB's transactional consistency.

We demonstrate that a certain operator, when applied to the chromatic symmetric function of a single variable, yields an $s_{1} (\mathbf{y})$ multiplied by a positively weighted sum of Schur functions of the second kind. Furthermore, we find that the associated combinatorial coefficients are non-negative integers, which represent the count of inverse Kostka tableaux of shape $\lambda=(l_1,\dots,l_s)$. This result is supported by defining inverse Kostka tableaux as a new class of combinatorial objects, which are shown to be in bijection with semistandard tableaux of the same shape, thereby establishing their $s_{1} (\mathbf{y})$-positivity. We also establish the $s_{1} (\mathbf{y})$-positivity of the classical Grobner polynomials for the intersection of the Coxeter arrangement of type $A_{n-1}$ and the hyperplanes $x_{i}=x_{j}$ for $1\leq j<i\leq n$. Additionally, we extend our result to show the $s_{1} (\mathbf{y})$-positivity of the chromatic symmetric functions for the intersections of the Coxeter arrangement of type $A_{n-1}$ with the hyperplanes $x_{i}=0$ for $x_{n} = 0$.
